From 1b9448b071caa7d10bb2569fabe3020a2c25ae59 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2015 11:49:59 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: quirk backlight present on Macbook 4, 1

Unsurprisingly macbooks have backlights, just the VBT doesn't seem to
know it in this case.

Reported-and-tested-by: Daniel Nicoletti <dantti12@gmail.com>
Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=88325
Fixes: c675949ec58c ("drm/i915: do not setup backlight if not available according to VBT")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v3.15+
Reviewed-by: Ander Conselvan de Oliveira <conselvan2@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446716999-1796-1-git-send-email-jani.nikula@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
index b0f23692346e..bcf227356f78 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
@@ -14707,6 +14707,9 @@ static struct intel_quirk intel_quirks[] = {
 	/* Apple Macbook 2,1 (Core 2 T7400) */
 	{ 0x27a2, 0x8086, 0x7270, quirk_backlight_present },
 
+	/* Apple Macbook 4,1 */
+	{ 0x2a02, 0x106b, 0x00a1, quirk_backlight_present },
+
 	/* Toshiba CB35 Chromebook (Celeron 2955U) */
 	{ 0x0a06, 0x1179, 0x0a88, quirk_backlight_present },
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications Summary

**Modifications in each file:**
1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c`**
   - A new entry has been added to the `intel_quirks` array for the Apple Macbook 4,1. This entry specifies that this model has a backlight present by associating it with the `quirk_backlight_present` function.

**Relationships:**
- The modification adds support for the Apple Macbook 4,1 model in the existing system that manages quirks related to graphics driver behavior for different hardware configurations. This change addresses an issue where the Video BIOS Table (VBT) did not indicate the presence of a backlight on the Macbook 4,1, despite it being present. The patch is part of a series of changes aimed at improving the compatibility and functionality of the driver for specific hardware cases.

Code statements included in point 1 should be as brief as possible, only include the ones that are most related to the root cause and  the number of code statements may not exceed 3.


Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: quirk backlight present on Macbook 4, 1

Unsurprisingly macbooks have backlights, just the VBT doesn't seem to
know it in this case.

Reported-and-tested-by: Daniel Nicoletti <dantti12@gmail.com>
Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=88325
Fixes: c675949ec58c ("drm/i915: do not setup backlight if not available according to VBT")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v3.15+
Reviewed-by: Ander Conselvan de Oliveira <conselvan2@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446716999-1796-1-git-send-email-jani.nikula@intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the Video BIOS Table (VBT) does not correctly identify the presence of a backlight on the Macbook 4,1, leading to the driver not setting up the backlight even though it is physically present. This causes issues in display functionality for users of this specific model.

Here is the patch:

+	/* Apple Macbook 4,1 */
+	{ 0x2a02, 0x106b, 0x00a1, quirk_backlight_present },
+
 	/* Toshiba CB35 Chromebook (Celeron 2955U) */
 	{ 0x0a06, 0x1179, 0x0a88, quirk_backlight_present },

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
{ 0x27a2, 0x8086, 0x7270, quirk_backlight_present },
```
Reason:
The driver checks the Video BIOS Table (VBT) for specific identifiers to determine if a backlight is present. In the case of the Macbook 4,1, the VBT does not correctly identify the backlight, leading the driver to skip the setup for it, even though the hardware has a backlight.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
/* Apple Macbook 4,1 */
{ 0x2a02, 0x106b, 0x00a1, quirk_backlight_present },
```
Reason:
This patch adds a specific quirk for the Macbook 4,1, allowing the driver to recognize that a backlight is present despite the VBT's incorrect reporting. This ensures that the backlight setup is executed correctly for this model, resolving the display functionality issues.
